name: Rhinoplasty tip-narrowing sutures

lead: Tip-narrowing sutures give a broad or bulbous nasal tip a slimmer, more refined shape. The stitches reshape the cartilage rather than cutting it away, so the tip is narrowed while the tissue stays in place.

Sutures placed in the lower lateral cartilages pull and hold the folded cartilage in a tighter shape, narrowing the tip, and the change shows once swelling settles. General rhinoplasty references describe sutures as a standard way to narrow a wide tip; little published research has looked at the technique on its own.

paras: It is performed by a surgeon as one step within a rhinoplasty, often alongside other tip or bridge work. The nose is swollen at first, and the narrower tip becomes clear as healing progresses over the following months.
Risks are those of rhinoplasty in general, including revision surgery in roughly 5 to 20 percent of operations. It is a surgical procedure performed under anesthesia.

angle.text: People with a broad or bulbous nasal tip get stitches that reshape and narrow the tip cartilage without removing it, giving a slimmer, more refined nose. The change is visible once healing is complete. Little dedicated research on the technique alone has been published.

lead: Tip-narrowing sutures are stitches placed in the lower lateral cartilages of the nose during rhinoplasty to reshape and narrow a broad or bulbous tip without removing cartilage. General rhinoplasty references describe sutures as a way to narrow a wide tip by tightening the folded cartilage apex [1].

The sources reviewed contain little dedicated published research on the technique itself, so this article is short. Registered studies list suture-related tip work alongside grafts, but none was found specifically testing tip sutures alone.
infobox: Primary and revision rhinoplasty (often open approach)
Refine a wide or bulbous nasal tip

paras: Surgeons can narrow the tip by suturing the cartilage rather than resecting it, and open rhinoplasty is described as giving better visualization and precision for tip work [1]. Suture work is often combined with grafts such as the columellar strut.

No studies found for tip-narrowing sutures specifically. Registered trials of related tip surgery include a study of lateral crural steal with a columellar strut (NCT07317947, 22 participants, recruiting) [2] and a comparison of septal advancement flap and columellar strut effect on the tip (NCT06370455, 30 participants, completed) [3].
Risks are those of rhinoplasty in general; revision surgery accounts for roughly 5 to 20 percent of operations, with pinched or asymmetric tips among reasons cited [1].
